content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has published a document titled Checklist of Prerequisites to Country Implementation of Xpert MTB/RIF and Key Action Points at Country Level. This document outlines the necessary steps and considerations for countries planning to implement the Xpert MTB/RIF diagnostic assay, a tool designed for the rapid detection of tuberculosis (TB) and rifampicin resistance. Below is a professional summary of the key points and recommendations from the document: 1. Background: Early and improved detection of TB, including smear-negative TB often associated with HIV, and the expanded capacity to diagnose multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB), are global priorities for TB control. The emergence of extensively drug-resistant TB (XDR-TB), institutional transmission, and high mortality rates in patients with MDR-TB and HIV co-infection underscore the urgency for rapid diagnostic methods. In December 2010, WHO endorsed the Xpert MTB/RIF assay and recommended its phased rollout within national TB management plans. A global consultation convened by WHO in December 2010 reached consensus on interim diagnostic algorithms, the positioning of Xpert MTB/RIF in health services, and programmatic considerations for its implementation. 2. Policy Recommendations: Xpert MTB/RIF should be used as the initial diagnostic test for individuals suspected of having MDR-TB or HIV-associated TB (strong recommendation). In settings where MDR-TB or HIV is of lesser concern, Xpert MTB/RIF may be considered as a follow-up test to microscopy, particularly for smear-negative specimens (conditional recommendation due to resource implications). Conventional microscopy, culture, and drug susceptibility testing (DST) remain necessary for monitoring treatment progress and detecting resistance to drugs other than rifampicin. In settings where rifampicin resistance is rare, Xpert MTB/RIF results indicating resistance should be confirmed by conventional DST or line-probe assays (LPA). 3. Operational Requirements for Implementation: Successful implementation of Xpert MTB/RIF requires: Stable electricity supply and appropriate infrastructure (e.g., secure premises, adequate storage for cartridges at 2–28°C). Trained personnel with basic computer literacy and knowledge of laboratory procedures. Biosafety precautions similar to those for sputum smear microscopy. Annual calibration of the GeneXpert instrument by a commercial supplier. 4. Checklist of Prerequisites: Epidemiological Data: Availability of data on MDR-TB and HIV-associated TB prevalence to prioritize placement of the technology. Diagnostic Policy Reform: Plans to modify existing diagnostic algorithms to incorporate Xpert MTB/RIF testing. Laboratory Network: Infrastructure: Stable electricity, secure premises, and adequate storage for cartridges. Treatment Capacity: Sufficient capacity to treat identified TB and MDR-TB patients in line with international recommendations. Financing: Procurement: Streamlined importation procedures for equipment and consumables, including regulatory registration or waivers. 5. Key Action Points for Implementation: Update national diagnostic strategies to include Xpert MTB/RIF testing and identify appropriate placement within the diagnostic network. Develop systems for same-day reporting of results to clinics and regular reporting to WHO. Forecast and procure equipment and consumables, ensuring buffer stock to cover at least three months of expected workload. Validate the system using the Global Laboratory Initiative (GLI) validation kit and report results to WHO/GLI. Perform annual calibration of modules or after 2,000 tests per module. 6. Sample Budget: The document includes a sample budget to assist countries in planning for the financial requirements of implementing Xpert MTB/RIF. This comprehensive checklist and set of recommendations aim to guide countries in the systematic rollout of Xpert MTB/RIF, optimizing its use and benefits in diverse epidemiological and resource settings.
